subtitle: From Purdah to Ladyland: A School, a Pen, a New Sky for Muslim Women

panels.shot: epic three-quarter view, low-angle, with Rokeya standing between a veiled zenana doorway and a bright school courtyard, half in shadow, half in light
panels.action: Begum Rokeya Sakhawat Hussain stands poised between a darkened inner courtyard with lattice screens and a sunlit scene of young girls reading under a banyan tree, her hand resting on a stack of worn books.

dialogue.text: In an age when many said Muslim women must not learn, Begum Rokeya Sakhawat Hussain dreamed of Ladyland—and then built real schools from that dream.

i18n.hi: जब लोग कहते थे मुसलमान औरतें न पढ़ें, बेगम रोकैया सखावत हुसैन ने लेडीलैंड का सपना देखा – और उसी से असली स्कूल खड़े कर दिए।

panels.shot: slow push-in from above on a child in purdah, framed by carved wooden lattice, a sliver of sky beyond
panels.action: A young Rokeya, her face half-veiled, sits behind a carved wooden screen in a Rangpur zenana, clutching a slate as a faint strip of blue sky glows beyond the courtyard wall.

dialogue.text: Rangpur, around 1890. In a house where girls were kept from books, a quiet girl presses a slate to her chest and listens for the sound of forbidden letters.

i18n.hi: रंगपुर, करीब 1890. उस घर में जहाँ लड़कियाँ किताबों से दूर रहती हैं, एक चुप सी बच्ची तख्ती सीने से लगाकर मन ही मन उन मनहूस, मनाही वाली इबारतें सुनती है।

panels.shot: intimate over-the-shoulder, candlelit, on Rokeya tracing letters, a door slightly ajar as if danger could enter
panels.action: In a dim room lit by a single oil lamp, teenage Rokeya sits close to the floor, secretly tracing Bengali letters on paper while a shadow of a stern elder falls across the half-open door.

dialogue.text: Her brothers teach her Bengali and English in secret, against the wishes of elders who fear that education will make women restless and disobedient.

i18n.hi: भाई उसे छुपकर बांग्ला और अंग्रेज़ी सिखाते हैं, उन बुज़ुर्गों की नापसंद के बावजूद जो डरते हैं कि पढ़ाई से औरतें बेचैन और नाफरमान हो जाएँगी।

panels.shot: side profile medium close-up, Rokeya listening, a male figure in the background gesturing dismissively
panels.action: Rokeya sits with lowered eyes near a doorway as an unseen elder male hand in the background gestures sharply, indicating refusal, while a folded paper with English words peeks from her palm.

dialogue.text: The arguments echo through the house: ‘Bengali is useless for girls, English is dangerous.’ But the letters have already taken root in her mind.

i18n.hi: घर भर में बहस गूंजती है: ‘लड़कियों को बांग्ला बेकार, अंग्रेज़ी ख़तरनाक।’ मगर अक्षर तो पहले ही उसके मन में जड़ें जमा चुके हैं।

panels.shot: wedding-day wide shot, soft focus, Rokeya in bridal attire looking sideways toward a stack of books on a low table
panels.action: In Bhagalpur, Rokeya in bridal finery sits in a modest room, her gaze drawn away from the ceremonial tray toward a small pile of books resting by a window.

dialogue.text: In 1898 she marries Sakhawat Hossain, a modern-minded deputy magistrate. In this new house, books are not hidden enemies but honoured guests.

i18n.hi: 1898 में उसकी शादी होती है सखावत हुसैन से, एक तरक्कीपसंद डिप्टी मजिस्ट्रेट। इस नए घर में किताबें दुश्मन नहीं, इज़्ज़तदार मेहमान हैं।

panels.shot: gentle two-shot, profile, with Rokeya seated and an unseen husband’s hand pointing to a line in a book
panels.action: In a quiet inner room, Rokeya sits with a book open on her lap while a man’s hand, likely her husband’s, points to a line as she follows the script with intense concentration.

dialogue.text: Her husband urges her to write, to learn better Bengali, to use the very language some had denied her. She begins to shape essays from the pain of seclusion.

i18n.hi: शौहर उसे लिखने को कहता है, बांग्ला और निखारने को, उसी ज़बान में कलम चलाने को जो कभी उससे छीनी गई थी। वह अपने हिजाब के दर्द को निबंधों का रूप देना शुरू करती है।

panels.shot: overhead shot of a desk with inkpot, manuscript pages titled 'Matichur' in Bengali script, and Rokeya’s hand writing
panels.action: Rokeya sits cross-legged by a low desk, dipping a pen into a small inkpot as neat Bengali lines grow on pages gathered under the title ‘Matichur’, while household utensils lie nearby.

dialogue.text: Around 1904, her essays later collected as Matichur take form—sharp, clear critiques of customs that lock women away, written in simple Bengali so ordinary women can read them.

i18n.hi: करीब 1904 में उसके लेख ‘मातीचूर’ बनकर उभरते हैं—तेज़, साफ़ हमले उन रिवाज़ों पर जो औरतों को बंद रखती हैं, सादा बांग्ला में ताकि आम औरतें भी पढ़ सकें।

panels.shot: medium shot, Rokeya at a table with English periodicals, steam from a teacup rising, night outside
panels.action: At a small table, Rokeya sits by a lantern with English magazines scattered around, her pen poised over a fresh sheet as rain streaks against the dark window.

dialogue.text: Then she turns to English, not to escape her world but to reach further. In 1905 she sends a strange, bold story to The Indian Ladies’ Magazine.

i18n.hi: फिर वह अंग्रेज़ी की ओर मुड़ती है, भागने को नहीं, और दूर तक पहुँचने को। 1905 में वह एक अजीब, दिलेर कहानी ‘द इंडियन लेडीज़ मैगज़ीन’ को भेजती है।

panels.shot: imaginative split-scene: Rokeya writing on one side, Ladyland cityscape in clouds on the other, with solar panels and flying cars suggested softly
panels.action: On one side Rokeya writes intently, while above her head the page blossoms into a vision of Ladyland—tree-lined streets, women in flowing veils directing machines powered by stylised suns.

dialogue.text: In Sultana’s Dream, she imagines Ladyland, where purdah is reversed, men stay indoors, and women scholars harness solar power to end war and fear.

i18n.hi: ‘सुल्तानाज़ ड्रीम’ में वह लेडीलैंड गढ़ती है, जहाँ पर्दा उलट गया है, मर्द घरों में कैद हैं, और औरत आलिम सूरज की ताकत से जंग और दहशत ख़त्म कर देती हैं।

panels.shot: wider shot of a Calcutta or Bhagalpur drawing room, women in varied attire listening as one reads a printed magazine
panels.action: In a modest drawing room, a woman in a sari reads aloud from a printed magazine as a small circle of veiled and unveiled women lean in, while Rokeya listens from the side with a quiet smile.

dialogue.text: Across Bengal, women hear these English words and smile at their daring. But Rokeya knows that dreams on paper are not enough; real girls still sit behind real screens.

i18n.hi: पूरे बंगाल में औरतें ये अंग्रेज़ी लफ्ज़ पढ़कर मुस्कुराती हैं, उनकी जुर्रत पर दंग। मगर रोकैया जानती है, काग़ज़ के ख़्वाब काफी नहीं; असली लड़कियाँ अब भी असली परदों के पीछे बैठी हैं।

panels.shot: somber close-up, low light, Rokeya holding a folded letter, eyes moist but steady
panels.action: In Bhagalpur, Rokeya sits alone, gripping a folded official letter, her eyes shining with tears as the faint outline of her husband’s absent figure is suggested in the background.

dialogue.text: Soon after, grief strikes. Her husband dies, leaving her widowed, with limited means. His encouragement remains, but his salary is gone.

i18n.hi: थोड़े ही दिनों में सदमा टूट पड़ता है। शौहर का इंतक़ाल हो जाता है, वह कम रसद के साथ बेवा रह जाती है। उसका हौसला बचा है, उसकी तनख़्वाह नहीं।

panels.shot: determined medium shot, Rokeya standing before a bare room with a chalkboard, a few mats on the floor
panels.action: Rokeya stands in a bare Bhagalpur room with rough walls, a simple chalkboard leaning behind her and a few woven mats laid out, as if she is imagining children filling the space.

dialogue.text: From her husband’s small savings and her own resolve, she opens Sakhawat Memorial Girls’ School in Bhagalpur in 1909—starting with almost nothing but a rented room and a few pupils.

i18n.hi: शौहर की थोड़ी बचत और अपनी अड़िग नीयत से वह 1909 में भागलपुर में सखावत मेमोरियल गर्ल्स’ स्कूल खोलती है—बस एक किराए के कमरे और चंद बच्चियों से शुरुआत।

panels.shot: busy medium-wide shot, Rokeya sweeping the classroom floor at dawn, her sari hitched for work, a kettle in the corner
panels.action: At dawn, Rokeya sweeps the dusty classroom floor, her sari tucked for ease, a kettle boiling on a small stove nearby as sunlight creeps across the empty mats.

dialogue.text: She cleans the rooms herself, cooks, writes, teaches. There is no invisible army behind her—only her own labour and a few loyal helpers.

i18n.hi: वह खुद कमरे साफ़ करती है, खाना बनाती है, लिखती है, पढ़ाती है। उसके पीछे कोई ग़ैबी फ़ौज नहीं—बस उसकी अपनी मेहनत और चंद वफ़ादार मददगार।

panels.shot: heated courtyard scene, low angle, with male relatives in discussion and Rokeya standing firm near the doorway of the school
panels.action: In a small courtyard, two older men argue in raised voices while Rokeya stands by the doorway of the school, her posture firm yet respectful, the signboard just visible behind her shoulder.

dialogue.text: Family members protest. Some say a widow has no business running a school, that educating girls in this way is dangerous. She answers calmly, citing justice and duty from within her own faith.

i18n.hi: अपने ही लोग एतराज़ करते हैं। कोई कहता है बेवा को स्कूल चलाने का क्या हक़, लड़कियों की ऐसी तालीम ख़तरनाक है। वह ठंडी आवाज़ में, अपने ही मज़हब की रोशनी से, इंसाफ़ और फ़र्ज़ का हवाला देती है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a classroom, girls of different ages seated, Rokeya writing the word 'Knowledge' in Bengali on a slate
panels.action: Inside the classroom, girls in simple veils sit with slates as Rokeya writes a Bengali word meaning knowledge on a large slate, her expression gentle but focused.

dialogue.speaker: begum_rokeya_sakhawat_hussain
dialogue.text: This is your right. No one gives it as charity.

i18n.hi: ये तुम्हारा हक़ है। कोई इसे खैरात में नहीं देता।

panels.shot: transition shot, train puffing through countryside, Rokeya visible in a carriage window, city skyline ahead
panels.action: A steam train cuts through the Bengal countryside; through a carriage window, Rokeya’s composed face is seen watching as distant rooftops of Calcutta rise under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: By 1911 she moves the school to Calcutta, seeking more students, more support—and facing the sharper scrutiny of a big city.

i18n.hi: 1911 तक वह स्कूल को कलकत्ता ले आती है, ज़्यादा छात्राएँ और मदद तलाशने—और बड़े शहर की तेज़ नज़रें भी झेलने।

panels.shot: wide urban courtyard shot, old Calcutta building with signboard, girls entering, Rokeya at the threshold
panels.action: In a congested Calcutta lane, a weathered building bears a modest sign as veiled girls slip through its gate; Rokeya stands at the threshold, welcoming them inside.

dialogue.text: Sakhawat Memorial Girls’ School grows slowly. Fees are low, funds uncertain. Yet year by year, more Muslim families trust their daughters to this unusual widow’s care.

i18n.hi: सखावत मेमोरियल गर्ल्स’ स्कूल धीरे-धीरे बढ़ता है। फ़ीस कम, पैसा अनिश्चित। फिर भी हर साल ज़्यादा मुसलमान ख़ानदान अपनी बेटियों को इस नायाब बेवा के हवाले करने लगते हैं।

panels.shot: meeting-room medium wide, with a circle of Muslim women seated on mats, Rokeya addressing them
panels.action: In a simple hall, Muslim women sit in a circle on mats, some faces veiled, as Rokeya speaks from the front, her hands gently outstretched in explanation.

dialogue.text: In 1916 she founds the Anjuman-e-Khawateen-e-Islam, an organisation of Muslim women to spread education, secure employment, and discuss social reform within a shared ethical language.

i18n.hi: 1916 में वह अंजुमन-ए-ख़वातीन-ए-इस्लाम बनाती है—मुस्लिम औरतों की जमात, ताकि तालीम फैले, रोज़गार मिले, और इस्लामी अख़्लाक़ की ज़बान में समाजी इस्लाह पर बात हो।

panels.shot: close-up on Rokeya’s hands distributing small coins and pamphlets to a younger woman
panels.action: Rokeya presses a few coins and a folded pamphlet into the hands of a younger woman, who looks both anxious and hopeful, while other women watch in the background.

dialogue.text: They raise small funds, find jobs, counsel new widows, help girls stay in school. The work is not glamorous; it is patient, practical, stitched from many tiny acts.

i18n.hi: वे थोड़े-थोड़े चंदे जुटाती हैं, नौकरियाँ ढूँढती हैं, नई बेवाओं की राह दिखाती हैं, लड़कियों को स्कूल में टिकाए रखती हैं। काम शोहरत वाला नहीं; सब्र वाला, हकीक़ी, छोटी-छोटी कोशिशों से बुना हुआ।

panels.shot: intense writing close-up, Rokeya’s face lit by lamp, Bengali manuscript titled 'Abarodhbasini' visible
panels.action: Late at night, Rokeya writes by lamp, a stack of pages bearing the Bengali title ‘Abarodhbasini’ nearby, as shadows from the window lattice fall across her desk.

dialogue.text: Her Bengali prose sharpens. In Abarodhbasini, completed by 1931, she records real stories of women crushed by extreme seclusion, naming the cruelty without flinching.

i18n.hi: उसकी बांग्ला गद्य और नुकीली हो जाती है। ‘आबरुधबासिनी’ में, जो 1931 तक मुकम्मल होती है, वह हद से ज़्यादा पर्दे में कुचली गई औरतों की सच्ची दास्तानें लिखती है, ज़ुल्म को बेझिझक नाम लेकर।

panels.shot: montage-style wide, ghosted images of various women in different domestic spaces, overlaid behind Rokeya’s silhouette
panels.action: Behind Rokeya’s steady silhouette, faint scenes appear: a woman locked in a dark inner room, another peering through a tiny window, another secretly reading by a hearth.

dialogue.text: She insists that faith does not demand such cages, that justice and compassion within her own tradition call for women to step into education and public life.

i18n.hi: वह ज़ोर देती है कि ईमान ऐसे पिंजरे नहीं माँगता, कि उसकी अपनी रिवायत में इंसाफ़ और रहम औरतों को तालीम और सार्वजनिक ज़िंदगी में क़दम रखने की पुकार करते हैं।

panels.shot: classroom wide shot, later years, older Rokeya seated as students recite, calendar on wall hinting late 1920s
panels.action: In a later-year classroom, an older Rokeya sits at a desk while a row of girls recite from textbooks, a simple calendar on the wall suggesting the late 1920s.

dialogue.text: By the late 1920s, dozens of girls have passed through her school. Some become teachers, some clerks, some simply mothers who insist their own daughters must study.

i18n.hi: 1920 के आख़िर तक उसकी स्कूल से दरजन भर लड़कियाँ निकल चुकी हैं। कोई टीचर बनती है, कोई क्लर्क, कोई बस ऐसी माँ जो अपनी बेटियों के पढ़ने पर अडिग रहती है।

panels.shot: gentle close-up of Rokeya watching a girl write at a desk, pride and fatigue in her eyes
panels.action: Rokeya watches quietly as a young girl bends over her notebook, the older woman’s face lined with fatigue yet lit with a soft, satisfied pride.

dialogue.text: She never sees a fully equal world. Poverty remains, resistance remains. But between the zenana of her childhood and this classroom, a long bridge has been built.

i18n.hi: उसे मुकम्मल बराबरी वाली दुनिया नहीं नसीब होती। गरीबी भी रहती है, मुक़ाबला भी। मगर बचपन की ज़नाने से इस क्लासरूम तक एक लंबा पुल बन चुका है।

panels.shot: final reflective wide shot, rooftop view at dawn, Rokeya looking out over Calcutta as faint images of Ladyland superimpose in clouds
panels.action: At dawn on a Calcutta rooftop, Rokeya stands wrapped in a shawl, gazing over the waking city as soft, cloud-like visions of Ladyland’s peaceful streets float above the horizon.

dialogue.text: Begum Rokeya turned a secret education into essays, a utopian dream into a school, and a life in purdah into a path so that others could walk out of seclusion under their own sun.

i18n.hi: बेगम रोकैया ने छुपकर मिली तालीम को निबंध बनाया, एक ख़्वाबी लेडीलैंड को स्कूल में बदला, और पर्दे की ज़िंदगी से ऐसी राह निकाली कि और लोग भी अपने सूरज के नीचे इस कैद से बाहर चल सकें।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Purdah to Ladyland: A School, a Pen, a New Sky for Muslim Women
subtitle_i18n.hi: परदे से लेडीलैंड तक: एक स्कूल, एक कलम, मुसलमान औरतों के लिए नया आसमान
